extraction.notes: 1. Witness B spoken vs. marked position (Depo 09:04, 27:04, 27:05): Earlier in her testimony (Depo 09:04) Witness B states she was waiting at the bench shelter in front of the store, and at Depo 27:04 she says aloud 'I was over by the corner, near the shelter.' However, on the video at Depo 27:05 she places her red 'X' on Exhibit 4 at the pavement corner where the US-27A eastbound shoulder meets the east edge of NE 140th Court (approximately [2.0, 6.0] m from the AOI), about 7 m northwest of the bench shelter ([8.0, 10.0] m). 2. Witness B prior statements vs. deposition claim (police_report.txt p.3; Depo 27:47, 28:17, 28:50-29:27): At the deposition Witness B insists she had a clear, unobstructed view of the front of the car during the last second right up until it went under the trailer. In her brief oral statement at the scene (police_report.txt p.3) and her written statement a few days later (Depo 29:16), she did not state that she watched the car all the way to impact. Moreover, because the tractor had already entered NE 140th Court and the semitrailer was stretched across both eastbound lanes (Depo 24:09) while the car was in the outside (southernmost) eastbound lane, the geometry between her marked position [2.0, 6.0] and the approaching car should be checked for line-of-sight / perspective consistency. 3. Inferred eye heights: Eye heights are not stated in the evidence and are inferred as 1.2 m for Witness A (car driver), 1.6 m for Witness B (standing adult pedestrian per Depo 27:24), and ~1.5 m (or 1.2-1.8 m) for Witness C (seated in a pickup truck). 4. Inferred positions along Z (north-south) for Witnesses A and C: Derived from US-27A road cross-section geometry in facts.txt F6-F8 (AOI at center of EB outside lane; EB inside lane -3.66 m; 78 ft / 23.77 m median + turn lane + shoulders from -5.49 m to -29.26 m; WB inside lane center ~ -26.8 m; WB outside lane center ~ -30.5 m).

findings.summary: Witness B could not have watched the car up to impact from where she marked she was standing: Vehicle T's tractor, then its semitrailer, block her view from about t=9.1s.
findings.detail: Her eye-level render at t=9.9s shows the tractor filling the direction of the approaching car; the overhead render shows the truck crossing between her X and the eastbound lanes. The ray-cast agrees (blocked by veh_T_tractor, 28.3 m to the car). She testified "I had a clear view of the car the whole way in. I watched it right up until the moment it hit. Nothing was in the way." (Depo 27:46).

results.subject: veh_A
results.detail: The driver of Vehicle A had a continuous line of sight to Vehicle T for 10.43 s before impact (t=0.00–10.43 s), from the start of the reconstructed timeline, so this is a lower bound. Typical perception-reaction time is 1.5 s (range 1–2.5 s). Time available is more than the 2.5 s upper bound, so there was time to perceive and begin reacting. Vehicle T came within 3 m of the centerline of this driver's remaining path 2.88 s before impact. Kinematic estimate from the reconstructed geometry; it does not account for attention, conspicuity, glare or expectation.
